results.title: Normalized density family
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space with a measure $\mu$ and let $\Theta$ be a set of parameters. A normalized density family on $\Omega$ indexed by $\Theta$ with dominating measure $\mu$ consists of a function $f_\theta : \Omega \to [0, \infty]$ for each $\theta \in \Theta$ such that $f_\theta$ is $\mu$-almost everywhere measurable and $\int_\Omega f_\theta \, d\mu = 1$.

results.title: Normalized density families are determined by their densities
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ and $G$ be normalized density families on a measurable space $\Omega$ with the same parameter set $\Theta$ and the same dominating measure $\mu$. If for every $\theta \in \Theta$ and every $x \in \Omega$ the density of $F$ at $\theta$ and the density of $G$ at $\theta$ take the same value at $x$, then $F = G$.

results.summary: Let $F$ be a normalized density family on a measurable space $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$, dominating measure $\mu$ and densities $f_\theta$. results.title: Population laws are probability measures

results.title: Likelihood of an iid sample
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$ and densities $f_\theta$ for $\theta \in \Theta$. For a sample size $n$, a parameter $\theta \in \Theta$ and a sample $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}) \in \Omega^n$, the iid likelihood of $\theta$ at $x$ is $L_n(\theta; x) = \prod_{i < n} f_\theta(x_i)$, a value in $[0, \infty]$. For $n = 0$ this is the empty product $1$.

results.title: PCF variables

results.title: PCF renamings
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ (lists of PCF types), a renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ is a map sending each variable of $\Gamma$ of type $A$, for every type $A$, to a variable of $\Delta$ of the same type $A$; it is the STLC notion of renaming at PCF types.

results.title: PCF numerals
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Injectivity of PCF numerals
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Weakening of PCF terms
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Identity PCF substitution
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Multi-step call-by-name reduction of PCF
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For closed PCF terms $t$ and $t'$ of the same type, $t \to^* t'$ holds when $t$ reduces to $t'$ in finitely many, possibly zero, one-step call-by-name reductions; that is, $\to^*$ is the reflexive transitive closure of one-step reduction.

results.title: PCF numerals are normal forms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the closed numeral $\mathrm{succ}^n\,\mathrm{zero}$ of type nat does not reduce: there is no closed term $t'$ such that $\mathrm{succ}^n\,\mathrm{zero}$ reduces to $t'$ in one call-by-name step.

results.title: PCF values are normal forms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $v$ is a closed PCF value of type $A$ (an abstraction or a numeral), then there is no closed term $t'$ such that $v$ reduces to $t'$ in one call-by-name step.

results.title: Determinism of PCF call-by-name reduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: One-step call-by-name reduction of closed PCF terms is deterministic: if a closed term $t$ of type $A$ reduces in one step to $t_1$ and also reduces in one step to $t_2$, then $t_1 = t_2$.

results.title: Big-step evaluation implies reduction in PCF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $v$ be closed PCF terms of type $A$. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-name semantics, then $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) call-by-name steps.

results.title: Backward reduction preserves evaluation in PCF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be closed PCF terms of type $A$. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one call-by-name step and $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-name semantics, then $t$ evaluates to $v$.

results.title: Reduction to a value implies big-step evaluation in PCF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $v$ be closed PCF terms of type $A$. If $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) call-by-name steps and $v$ is a value, then $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-name semantics.

results.title: Big-step evaluation agrees with small-step reduction in PCF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For closed PCF terms $t$ and $v$ of type $A$, $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-name semantics if and only if $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) call-by-name steps and $v$ is a value.

results.title: Soundness of the PCF denotational semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a PCF type and let $t$ and $v$ be closed terms of type $A$. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ under big-step call-by-name evaluation, then for every environment $\eta$ of the empty context, the denotations of $t$ and $v$ at $\eta$ are equal.

results.title: Closed PCF terms that evaluate to a numeral denote its value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a closed PCF term of the ground type of natural numbers and let $n$ be a natural number. If $t$ evaluates to the numeral for $n$, then for every environment $\eta$ of the empty context, the denotation of $t$ at $\eta$ is the defined element $n$ of the flat domain of partial natural numbers.

results.title: The least element approximates every term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every PCF type $A$ and every closed term $t$ of type $A$, the least element $\bot$ of the domain of $A$ formally approximates $t$.

results.title: Formal approximation is closed under suprema of chains
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a PCF type, $t$ a closed term of type $A$ and $(c_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ a chain in the domain of $A$. If every $c_i$ formally approximates $t$, then the supremum $\bigsqcup_i c_i$ formally approximates $t$.

results.title: Formal approximation is closed under head expansion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a PCF type, let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of type $A$, and let $d$ be an element of the domain of $A$. If $t$ evaluates to every closed term $v$ to which $t'$ evaluates, and $d$ formally approximates $t'$, then $d$ formally approximates $t$.

results.title: Computational adequacy for PCF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a closed PCF term of ground type $\mathsf{nat}$ and let $n$ be a natural number. If the denotation of $t$ in the empty environment is defined with value $n$, then $t$ evaluates to the numeral $\mathsf{succ}^n(\mathsf{zero})$.

results.title: Evaluation to a numeral agrees with the denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, a closed PCF term $t$ of ground type evaluates to the numeral $n$ if and only if the denotation of $t$ is the defined value $n$.

results.title: Termination agrees with definedness of the denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A closed PCF term $t$ of ground type evaluates to some term if and only if its denotation, an element of the flat domain of partial natural numbers, is defined.

results.title: Equal denotations are preserved by plugging into PCF contexts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $u$ be PCF terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$ with the same denotation, and let $C$ be a one-hole context whose hole takes terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$. Then the terms $C[t]$ and $C[u]$ obtained by plugging $t$ and $u$ into the hole of $C$ have the same denotation.

results.title: Equal denotations imply contextual equivalence in PCF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two PCF terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type in the same typing context have the same denotation, as continuous maps from environments to the domain of their type, then $t$ and $u$ are contextually equivalent.

results.title: Denotational approximation implies contextual approximation in PCF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $u$ be PCF terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$, and write $[\![s]\!]$ for the denotation of a term $s$. If $[\![t]\!]\eta \le [\![u]\!]\eta$ in the domain denoted by $A$ for every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, then $t$ contextually approximates $u$.

results.title: Contextual equivalence in PCF is reflexive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is contextually equivalent to itself.

results.title: Contextual equivalence in PCF is a congruence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $u$ be PCF terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$. If $t$ and $u$ are contextually equivalent, then for every one-hole context $D$ whose hole takes terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$, the terms $D[t]$ and $D[u]$ obtained by plugging $t$ and $u$ into the hole of $D$ are contextually equivalent.

results.title: Contextual approximation in PCF is reflexive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ contextually approximates itself.

results.title: Contextual equivalence is mutual contextual approximation in PCF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: PCF terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type in the same typing context are contextually equivalent if and only if $t$ contextually approximates $u$ and $u$ contextually approximates $t$.
